boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Walk-in views and trails at Niagara Falls State Park and nearby state-park areas; driving or paid attractions are optional and excluded.

cards.title: Walk Goat Island
cards.subtitle: Niagara Falls State Park
cards.notes: Enter on foot and follow the island paths at your own pace. Skip paid attractions and vehicle parking to keep this outing free.
cards.short_summary: A walk-in island stop between the river and the falls.
cards.evidence_claim: New York State Parks says Niagara Falls State Park is always free to walk into; its official map identifies Goat Island.
cards.source_title: Niagara Falls State Park — New York State Parks
cards.access_notes: Free when entering on foot; the state lists vehicle-use fees for certain parking lots.

cards.title: Cross to Three Sisters Islands
cards.subtitle: Niagara Falls State Park
cards.notes: Use the wooden walkways to reach the islands and pause for upstream river views. Bring what you need; no purchase is required.
cards.short_summary: Connected islands with a close look at the Canadian Rapids.
cards.evidence_claim: The park’s official page identifies Three Sisters Islands and its walkways; New York State Parks says the park is free to enter on foot.
cards.source_title: Overlooks & Vistas — Niagara Falls State Park
cards.access_notes: Walk into Niagara Falls State Park rather than using paid vehicle parking; no attraction ticket is needed for the islands.

cards.title: Meet at Prospect Point
cards.subtitle: Niagara Falls State Park
cards.notes: Set a meet-up point at the overlook, then take in the river and American Falls from the public park paths.
cards.short_summary: A named overlook facing the American Falls.
cards.evidence_claim: Niagara Falls State Park identifies Prospect Point as an overlook of the American Falls, and New York State Parks says walking into the park is free.
cards.source_title: Overlooks & Vistas — Niagara Falls State Park
cards.access_notes: Use walk-in park access; Maid of the Mist tours departing nearby require tickets and are not part of this hang.

cards.title: Pause at Terrapin Point
cards.subtitle: Goat Island, Niagara Falls State Park
cards.notes: Walk out to this named Goat Island viewpoint and take in the river from the public path. Keep clear of railings and posted areas.
cards.short_summary: A Goat Island viewpoint reached without a ticket.
cards.evidence_claim: The official New York State Parks map labels Terrapin Point within Niagara Falls State Park, which is free to enter on foot.
cards.access_notes: Walk into the park for free; avoid paid vehicle parking and ticketed attractions.

cards.title: Walk to Luna Island
cards.subtitle: Niagara Falls State Park
cards.notes: Use the marked park paths to reach Luna Island and take a short, no-ticket pause between the named falls viewpoints.
cards.short_summary: A small named island on the park’s pedestrian route.
cards.evidence_claim: The official New York State Parks map identifies Luna Island within Niagara Falls State Park; the park is free to walk into.
cards.access_notes: Free on foot; seasonal attractions nearby may charge separately.

cards.title: View American Falls
cards.subtitle: Niagara Falls State Park
cards.notes: Use the public park overlooks for a falls-viewing break. Keep the plan simple: walk in, use the paths, and skip ticketed rides.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission view of one of the park’s three named falls.
cards.evidence_claim: New York State Parks identifies American Falls among the three falls in Niagara Falls State Park and says the park is free to walk into.
cards.source_title: Niagara Falls State Park — New York State Parks
cards.access_notes: Walk-in park access is free; do not include paid attractions or vehicle parking.

cards.title: View Bridal Veil Falls
cards.subtitle: Niagara Falls State Park
cards.notes: Add this named falls view to a walk through the park. Stay on open public paths and treat paid Cave of the Winds access as optional.
cards.short_summary: A walk-in falls view beside the park’s ticketed attractions.
cards.evidence_claim: New York State Parks lists Bridal Veil Falls among the falls in Niagara Falls State Park and states that the park is free to walk into.
cards.source_title: Niagara Falls State Park — New York State Parks
cards.access_notes: Free on foot; Cave of the Winds is a separate ticketed attraction.

cards.title: View Horseshoe Falls
cards.subtitle: Niagara Falls State Park
cards.notes: Walk the public park paths for a shared view of Horseshoe Falls. Plan to arrive on foot if a strictly no-cost outing matters.
cards.short_summary: A pedestrian-accessible view of the park’s third named falls.
cards.evidence_claim: New York State Parks identifies Horseshoe Falls within Niagara Falls State Park and says the park is always free to walk into.
cards.source_title: Niagara Falls State Park — New York State Parks
cards.access_notes: Enter on foot for free; parking lots may have vehicle-use fees.

cards.title: Walk the Whirlpool overlooks
cards.subtitle: Niagara Falls State Park — Whirlpool Area
cards.notes: Use the trailheads and overlooks for a river-focused walk. Check current trail notices before leaving, and remain on open marked routes.
cards.short_summary: A state-park river overlook area with no entry or parking fee listed.
cards.evidence_claim: New York State Parks says the Whirlpool Area is free to enter and park and lists trail access there.
cards.source_title: Niagara Falls State Park — Whirlpool Area
cards.access_notes: Free to enter and park per New York State Parks; verify current trail closures before visiting.

cards.title: Walk Devil’s Hole overlooks
cards.subtitle: Niagara Falls, NY
cards.notes: Use the scenic overlooks or open hiking trails for a low-key outdoor stop. Review posted trail updates and avoid closed sections.
cards.short_summary: A no-fee state park with gorge views and trails.
cards.evidence_claim: New York State Parks lists no fee for general park usage and vehicle entry at Devil's Hole State Park.
cards.source_title: Devil's Hole State Park — New York State Parks
cards.access_notes: Open year-round; the state lists no fee for general park usage/vehicle entry. Check current trail-closure notices.
